title: Name variants and entity linking
capability: Participant-scoped alias binding at write (vocative and short form to canonical participant)
gap: Resolver sees only subject/object of extracted assertions; nickname table is a closed lexicon without a prefix/short-form rule; a bare given name against a full name is only pending_merge; vocatives and query names never use aliases; the reference run extracts nothing so nothing is resolved.
proposal: write.vocative_alias_v2: in the stamping step detect a greeting/vocative token and bind it to a participant by exact match, nickname table, or unique >=3-letter prefix of exactly one participant; set typed addressee, learn the alias (learned.alias marker), tag alias:<token>; optional read.alias_expand for the BM25 leg. Bind nothing when ambiguous.
plug_in: write path, stamping stage (before the window segmenter); optional read-side BM25 query expansion
model_calls: 0 per turn, window, session and read

measurements.what: turns with a short-form vocative of a speaker name
measurements.method: heuristic: greeting word + capitalised token that is a >=3-letter strict prefix of a speaker name

measurements.what: questions whose gold turn is in such a session / holds the short form

other_benchmarks: Useful for multi-party and user/assistant logs (OP-Bench personas, ConvoMem); neutral on PrefEval (one user); MAB-CR benefits through subject aliases at supersede. Rule on participants only, no dataset vocabulary; low overfitting risk.
risk: Wrong prefix bind when two participants share a prefix (mitigated by exactly-one rule); no privacy change; no text is edited.
test_plan: Unit tests in tests/unit/lib (invented participants Bramwell and Ilse): 'Hey Bram!' binds addressee Bramwell; 2-letter prefix binds nothing; Bram+Bramwell both present binds nothing; nickname-table pair Tomasz/Tomek binds. Precision check of the 74 detected turns against a local hand list. Slice fail_retrieval.

title: Decontextualise turns into standalone dated statements
capability: Turn restatement (standalone text, absolute date, resolved speaker) plus a deterministic index view
status: built-off (window_extract + W2 stack); index view missing

existing.key: write.envelope_v2, prompt_v2, temporal_v2, grounding_v2, coverage_v2 (S44, S62)
existing.file: src/memspine/derive/compile.py; temporal.py; temporal_stage.py; ground.py; grounding_stage.py; coverage.py

gap: A restated fact is a separate record competing in the pool; the index of the turn itself never improves (ingest/write.py:626 embeds record.content, there is no embed_text); no verdict exists for any write-v2 screen.
proposal: Step 1 write.index_view=context: deterministic embed/BM25 text '{speaker}, {session date}, {topic}: {text}' with the read-side resolved date, content and lineage unchanged. Step 2: the gated restate stage of OBS-03 writes a grounded derived child whose slot goes to the source turn (facts_to_sources).
plug_in: write path just before embedding (ingest/write.py:626) and the lexical indexer; step 2 in the window envelope stages after temporal (100) and grounding (200)

measurements.what: questions with a relative-time gold turn

other_benchmarks: Index view needs timestamps (BEAM, MAB-CR ordering); skipped when no source time exists (ConvoMem, PrefEval). Restatement helps first-person implicit preference turns. Risk: date tokens bias retrieval to same-date turns (screen on/off).
risk: Date in the embedding can reduce diversity; restatement hallucination handled by grounding.
test_plan: Model-free: index text equals the expected string; unknown date adds no token; content byte-identical. Slices fail_temporal, fail_retrieval.

title: Context carry-over within a session; when to rephrase
capability: Gated turn completion with an antecedent link (rule-scored incompleteness, one grounded call only for flagged windows)
gap: No decision about when a turn is incomplete; extraction runs for every window or none; CONTEXT is a read-only coreference aid, not overlap and not an edge; no refers_to link.
proposal: derive/standalone.py (pure): weighted incompleteness score (unresolved pronoun .4, deictic .4, back-reference .4, follow-up question .5, ellipsis .3, missing subject .2; missing time is resolved by rule, not rephrased); rephrase when score >= 0.5; complete turns (named entity + verb + >=6 words) score 0; pure reactions are linked, not rephrased; system/tool/echo skipped. Flagged window -> one window_extract call asking for standalone text and refers_to line numbers; W2-08 grounding drops any rewrite with an entity/number/date not in cited or known lines; stored as a derived child with a context lineage edge.
plug_in: write path: segmenter gate, then window_extract, envelope stages (grounding mandatory), derived-write door
model_calls: 0 for unflagged windows; 1 per flagged window (about 450 of 1095 six-turn windows on the dataset by the strict rule)

measurements.method: heuristic: dependent pronoun/deictic/back-reference <=20 words, or short follow-up question, or <=6 words, or reaction opener <=8 words

measurements.what: six-turn windows with an incomplete turn
questions with an incomplete gold turn
questions where the previous turn, not the gold turn, holds the question terms

other_benchmarks: Strong for user/assistant chat with short replies (BEAM, OP-Bench, ConvoMem); English-only rules need language_guard and fail closed. Syntactic rule, low overfitting risk.
risk: Highest hallucination risk of the set; grounding stage is mandatory (flag refuses to start without write.grounding_v2). Derived text inherits the strictest parent tier.
test_plan: Model-free unit tests: elliptical follow-up after an Ilse turn is flagged with the right antecedent; 'Congrats!' is link-only; a complete Noor turn scores 0; a rewrite adding an unseen place is dropped. Slices: new fail_context (21 wrong incomplete-gold questions) plus fail_retrieval.

title: Personal profile with attribute history
capability: Attribute-history profile with a typed registry (cardinality, sensitivity tier, consent purpose) shared by miner, ladder and card

existing.key: offline.session_close_v2, profile_card_v2 (O4-02, O4-07; S33, S46, S64)

gap: No default attribute registry (every attribute undeclared); value_history is a projection never rendered to the reader; the card has 5 coarse sections and 24 slots; extractor not wired to ask consent before writing sensitive attributes such as gender.
proposal: offline.person_attributes_v2: declarative registry (attribute -> cardinality, state/event, sensitivity tier, consent purpose) feeding integration_cardinality and the miner; sleep histories stage persists an attribute-timeline derived record per (person, attribute) with dated parents; read.profile_history renders 'attribute: A (until d1) -> B (from d2)' for persons and attributes the query contract targets; user-stated evidence only for active values, assistant-proposed stays tentative; sensitive tiers default-deny without a personalisation:profile grant.
plug_in: sleep stage (histories), derived-write door, read compose header (within profile_budget_share), consent registry at write
model_calls: no new calls: miner 1 per session and session-close call 2 (1 per session, 272 on the dataset) already specified; timeline build is CPU

measurements.what: questions worded as a state change
measurements.method: heuristic regex; the benchmark barely tests history

other_benchmarks: Most transferable item: PrefEval (preference through filler), ConvoMem (changing-fact, user-fact), MAB-CR (newest overrides), OP-Bench sycophancy/diversity. History half must be validated on MAB-CR, not LoCoMo. Registry is domain-neutral; low overfitting risk.
risk: Privacy is the main risk: default-deny for sensitive and special-category attributes, remote_llm_max_tier, erasure re-derives the timeline (LIB-09).
test_plan: Model-free: two lives_in values give a two-span chain, hobbies coexist, a gender write without a grant is refused and counted, render golden test. Slices: new fail_attr (33 wrong) and MAB-CR dev for history.

title: Layer 3: images and world knowledge
capability: Asset-grounded evidence record (caption note) plus opt-in labelled public enrichment

existing.key: [image: caption] folded into turn text (harness) ; reader grounded_v2/v3 caption line
read.external_evidence + read.external_v2 (R3-13, S23; read-time, generic questions only)

gap: A caption is just words in a turn: no typed image-evidence record, no relevance note, no write-time enrichment layer; external_v2 never plans a lookup for a personal question and takes no caption as input; S23 is inert as configured and egress is undecided.
proposal: write.caption_facts (rule, 0 calls): caption wrapper -> asset_note derived record 'speaker shared a photo: caption' with the turn as parent, tagged asset:caption. Opt-in write.enrich_external: for a caption with a proper-noun/title noun phrase, a privacy-filtered generic lookup stored as a labelled public layer-3 record (family = registrable domain, trust capped, parent = the caption note), rendered only in a separate block, never as a user fact.
plug_in: write path (derived-write door) for the note; enrichment as a sleep or on-read step through the external provider port
model_calls: 0 for caption notes; 1 lookup per enrichable caption, bounded by external_max_calls

measurements.what: questions whose evidence includes a caption turn

measurements.method: heuristic: question stems overlap caption, not spoken text

other_benchmarks: Caption note generalises to alt text/OCR logs; none of the target benchmarks carries images. Enrichment needs egress, a provider and a licence decision (web mode deferred by the owner). Least general item.
risk: Egress and licence; wrong identification contained in the labelled block.
test_plan: Model-free: wrapper -> one asset_note with no text the turn lacks; non-caption turn -> none; external planner refuses a personal-only contract. Slices fail_reader, new fail_caption (55).

title: Inference from memory, not only retrieval
capability: Shape-gated inference route (commit with a cited reason) plus evidence-seeking probes
status: partial (harness variants, planner probes built-off, no screen)

existing.key: reader prompts dated_infer, grounded_generic_infer, dated_world, routed (shape-v1)
reference prompt grounded: 'best-supported answer, even if indirect'

gap: (a) Reader: the clauses that commit are not gated by shape; grounded_v2 regressed (81.5 vs 86.7, 5 gained / 17 lost) because a yes/no rule leaked into when/what answers. (b) Retrieval: 28 answers have no gold turn in any leg because the evidence is indirect (an activity implying a preference). True HyDE leg not built.
proposal: read.inference_mode: when the contract says request=inference, append a commit-first clause with a one-line reason that cites a memory line (other shapes keep grounded byte-identical; answer marked inferred in the render; checker drops an answer citing a missing line). Probes: planner v2 restricted to inference reads yields 2 subqueries naming activities or traits that imply each option; rule fallback '{person} {option noun}' from the 'A or B' structure; fused as RRF legs.
plug_in: compose/reader prompt selection by contract; read spine probes (router) before the pool cut
model_calls: prompt: 0; probes: 1 planner call per inference-shaped read (about 5% of reads)

measurements.what: wrong answers in a refusal/'not mentioned' form
measurements.value: 28 over all categories, 14 inside open-domain wrong
measurements.method: heuristic regex on the answer text

other_benchmarks: High: PrefEval is the same task, ConvoMem implicit-connection/preference, OP-Bench sycophancy/diversity. Opposite risk on OP-Bench irrelevance probes (over-committing); guard with gate_v2, cat-5 slice and OP-Bench dev 60; average-led adoption rule.
risk: Moderate: over-commitment; mitigated by contract gate, citation check, inferred label.
test_plan: Model-free: contract classifies 'Would Noor prefer a national park or a theme park?' as inference; prompt builder returns the clause for it and the unchanged grounded text for a 'when did' question (golden hash); rule probe yields two probes; checker drops an answer citing line 99 of 5. Slices fail_reader, fail_retrieval, cat-5 guard, OP-Bench dev 60.

title: Session and window summaries
capability: Multi-resolution, topic-labelled summaries that lift to member turns
status: built-off (screens queued; S33 fired zero calls)

existing.key: write.window_extract=all (episode section: title, summary, narrative, topics) (S61)
offline.session_close_v2 (O4-02; S33; fires only from the window machinery)

gap: No window stride/overlap (segmentation: 'no overlap and no gap in NEW lines'); CONTEXT is a read-only coreference aid; topic is not required on every summary; nothing measured.
proposal: write.window_overlap_turns (default 0): windows of size N advance by N-overlap; overlapping turns eligible in both windows, evidence deduped by write_id; add topic (lower-case plural class) to the episode and session-summary schemas and use it as a view tag (view_tag_leg). Decide the overlap only after S31/S33/S61 show the episode leg finds evidence the turn legs miss.
plug_in: segmenter (LIB-14), episode section schema, sleep summary job
model_calls: windows of 4 stride 3: 1958 on the dataset vs 1095 for 6/6; session level: 272
other_benchmarks: Helps long topic-drifting logs (BEAM, ConvoMem); hurts precision if summaries displace raw turns, hence lift-to-turns. Low overfitting risk.
risk: Summary drift; episodes are grounded to cited lines and written as close paraphrase.
test_plan: Model-free: size 4 overlap 1 gives [1-4],[4-7],[7-10]; each turn deposited once; a fact citing turn 4 gets one write id. Slices fail_retrieval, fail_list.

title: Link new turns to older facts; synonym and paraphrase query expansion
capability: Backreference linking at write and multi-probe paraphrase retrieval at read
status: partial (all probes built-off, no screen; HyDE leg not built)

existing.key: read.planner=llm v2|v3; read.compose_rewrites; read.statement_probe; read.prf_expansion; read.multi_intent_split; read.bridge_hop; read.second_round; read.cluster_expand
existing.file: src/memspine/read/pipeline/router.py; compose/pipeline/windows.py:218; prompts/defaults/query_rewrite.yaml (HyDE passage prompt, no leg)

gap: No rule paraphrase/synonym probe, no HyDE leg, no backreference detection or refers_to edge; measurements show lexical mismatch is not the failure driver where the vector leg finds the gold.
proposal: read.paraphrase_probes: up to 2 probes per read (planner-v2 subqueries when bound, else rules: statement form + closed verb-synonym swaps), fused as RRF legs at weight 0.5. write.backref_link: rule-detect a backreference phrase, retrieve the best two earlier turns of the same pair by the embedding of the noun phrase after it, write a refers_to lineage edge above a calibrated floor; the antecedent rides with the hit.
plug_in: read spine probes (router) ; write path after stamping
model_calls: 0 by rules; 1 per read with the planner; backref: 1 vector query per backreference turn, 0 model calls

measurements.what: gold found by vector top10 but not BM25 top10
gold found by BM25 but not vector
zero content-word overlap question vs every gold turn

other_benchmarks: PrefEval implicit form and ConvoMem benefit (request never uses the preference's words); risk of extra injection on OP-Bench irrelevance probes, guarded by gate_v2. English-only verb list: language_guard.
risk: Low; probe noise bounded by weight and gate.
test_plan: Model-free: a question with 'suggest' yields a probe with 'recommended'; probe weight 0.5 in the fused output; backref detector fires on an invented 'book you suggested' turn and not on its negative list. Slices fail_retrieval, fail_fusion.

title: Plural and pronoun enrichment
capability: Referent annotation on facts (who 'they' and 'we' are, with a count for groups)

existing.key: window_extract rule 3 (never write he/she/they), persons field

gap: A group referent ('the kids') has no field: persons lists named people only; 'we' resolves to speaker plus unknown; unmeasured.
proposal: referents: [{surface, resolves_to, kind, count, source_turns}] on the restate item, required only for gate-flagged pronouns; grounding requires resolves_to and count to occur in cited or CONTEXT lines else the referent is dropped; render '[they = the kids (2)]' as an annotation beside the line, stored text unchanged.
plug_in: inside the OBS-03 restate stage (item schema + renderer)

measurements.what: turns with a plural pronoun and no named antecedent
questions with such a gold turn
turns with an unresolved third-person pronoun

other_benchmarks: More value for small readers and multi-party logs (family, team) than for a 9B on two-person logs; low overfitting risk, low gain here.
risk: A wrong referent is a visible error; grounding and drop-on-doubt bound it.
test_plan: Model-free: fake item 'they were scared' with CONTEXT 'Ilse's two children' passes; referent naming absent Bram fails; render golden test. Slice fail_context.

title: Multi-entity and multi-hop questions as map-reduce
capability: Query decomposition with per-entity retrieval quotas and deterministic combine operators
status: partial (retired: slot loop, fact chain; built-off, unscreened: agentic query loop, planner v3 persons)

existing.key: read.agentic (I67; trigger multi_hop) ; agentic_mode=slot and read.fact_chain RETIRED
read.deep_v2 + read.obligations (R3-12/R3-16; join, compare, count, list, order; S55, S56, S63)

gap: No decomposition into per-entity sub-questions and no combine step: one pooled search for a two-person question is dominated by the better-covered entity; the agentic loop searches again but has no entity quota or combine rule.
proposal: read.decompose_v2: (1) rule detection (>=2 targets that are participants or known entities plus a set operator, comparison, per-entity count or before/after; shared-event verbs without an operator are not decomposed); (2) map: one sub-read per entity with a person filter and an equal token quota, cap 3, parallel, one shared rerank pass; (3) reduce in code: evidence table (entity, value, source line, date) and operators intersection, union, difference, compare, count (distinct merged events), before/after; reader answers from the table; (4) a missing operand reports which entity lacks evidence (obligations hole).
plug_in: read spine after the request/contract stage and before the pool cut (router); combine in compose
model_calls: 0 extra for detection and map; 1 reader call as today; optional planner v3 persons +1

measurements.method: heuristic regex (both, in common, same, share, together, either, neither)

other_benchmarks: Rare in single-user logs (BEAM, ConvoMem); common in multi-party logs and MAB-CR multi-hop. Operator vocabulary is English: language_guard. Moderate overfitting risk for the vocabulary; the retired slot loop is the warning, so the first step is the 0-call version.
risk: Entity extraction errors from the question; latency of n sub-reads (cap 3, shared rerank); no hallucination path since the table quotes source lines.
test_plan: Model-free: detector on 'Which city have both Bram and Ilse visited?' -> intersection of two entity reads; 'What did Bram and Ilse do together?' -> not decomposed; operators on small tables (intersection, union, difference, count merges one event on one date, before/after); entity-quota test. Slices fail_list plus new fail_multi (43).

title: Dates on facts and context
capability: Event-time and said-time on every fact and context line, with precision and basis

existing.key: read.resolve_relative_dates, relative_dates_anchored, resolve_durations, order_by_time_for_ordering, temporal_leg_mentions ; [date] prefix (ref)
write.temporal_v2 (W2-14 anchor ladder; S62 on fail_temporal)

gap: For a non-relative event the only date on a line is the said-date; the happened-date is a read-time annotation on relative phrases and is lost once the line leaves context; event time lives on the extracted fact, not on the turn the reader sees; cross-fact ordering by event time is best effort.
proposal: Fold into OBS-02/03: the restate item carries happened (ISO, precision, basis explicit|relative|inferred|unknown) from the existing anchor ladder; render '[said d1 | happened d2]' for restated lines and the raw line plus [= date] otherwise; read.timeline_block: a compact sorted event list for questions whose contract time view is order or duration (span_line generalised to n events).
plug_in: window envelope stage 100 (existing) + renderer; compose header

measurements.what: temporal wrong with a relative-time gold turn

other_benchmarks: Matters wherever timestamps exist (BEAM temporal, MAB-CR ordering, LoCoMo-Plus); ConvoMem and PrefEval have none (skip). The 'week before' convention is LoCoMo's own: keep it behind relative_dates_anchored.
risk: Wrong happened-date shown with authority; precision and basis shown in the render.
test_plan: Model-free: LIB-01 tests plus a golden render of the two-clock line; ordering test on a three-event table. Slice fail_temporal.
